subject.title: feat: nameplate attention --wait blocks until the human acknowledges

question: Should Nameplate accept `--wait`, `--timeout`, and exit statuses 0/3/4 as a stable public CLI contract before the queued attention lifecycle is finalized?
rationale: This non-maintainer feature adds permanent scripting surface, while the related queue proposal may change whether newer alerts replace or follow active alerts and therefore affects the meaning of `superseded`.

options.title: Accept with queue compatibility
options.body: Approve the CLI contract now, require real behavior proof, and require the queued-handoff work to preserve request IDs and define supersession explicitly.

options.title: Integrate queueing first
options.body: Pause this PR until acknowledgment outcomes are implemented directly on the sequential request lifecycle.

options.title: Decline blocking mode
options.body: Keep attention fire-and-forget and avoid adding a long-lived exit-code protocol to the helper CLI.

recommendation.title: Accept with queue compatibility
recommendation.body: Approve the CLI contract now, require real behavior proof, and require the queued-handoff work to preserve request IDs and define supersession explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and most recently defined the attention lifecycle and is the strongest available owner for its permanent CLI and concurrency contract.
